citation: Wilson, S., Dickman, C., Hobson, R. & Sanderson, C. 2018. Oxyuranus microlepidotus. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2018: e.T42493150A42493160. Accessed on 15 May 2026.

actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species ranges from southwest Queensland and adjacent South Australia into central South Australia. There is an old record from the junction of the Murray and Darling Rivers. There is also an old record from Tindarre. There is no recent evidence for the species from New South Wales.
documentation.population: Mirtschin and Davis (1985) reported that most specimens have been collected from the flood plains and channels of the Diamantina River and Cooper Creek in Queensland. Most recent sightings have however been from around Coober Pedy (S. Macdonald, pers. obs.). Due to a lack of systematic survey effort for this species, population trends across its range are unknown. The population tends to fluctuate in response to changing densities of Long-haired Rats.
documentation.habitats: This species is found on the cracked dark soils of river overflows or floodplains and on lateritic gibber plains. It feeds on mammals, particularly the local long-haired rat (Rattus villosissimus), as well as birds and lizards. This is an oviparous species with clutches between 12-20 eggs. Captive individuals have been documented to reach sexual maturity at 16 months of age in males and 28 months in females. (Gow 1983, Shine and Covacevich 1983, Cogger 2014)
documentation.threats: This species may be impacted by a loss of its rodent food source, mainly because of predation by non-native predators (cats and foxes). In addition, future large-scale use of waterways for irrigating surrounding areas may impact both the soil structure preferred by this species, and its rodent prey.
documentation.measures: It is present in several protected areas. Additional research is needed into the extent and severity of threats to this species, particularly the depletion of food sources through the predation of cats and foxes on rats.
documentation.use_trade: This snake is collected for the pet trade from the wild and bred in captivity.
documentation.rationale: This species is listed as Least Concern, as it is widespread and overall it is not considered to be declining. Although the impact of potential threats requires further research, these are likely to be localized within the snake's range.
